sourcedFrom: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 (2026)
cleanIntro: The TiN CAN is SIG Sauer's lightweight rifle suppressor for bolt action rifles, rated for common .30 caliber ammunition; SIG recommends using it only on bolt guns. It threads straight onto the barrel on a HUB mount that takes a 7/8-in. wrench. SIG's book is plain about the inside: the TiN CAN needs no internal cleaning, and nothing past unscrewing a HUB tapered mount from the body is authorized. So nothing in this guide opens the can. The maintenance SIG publishes is the threads, the outside of the body and an inspection, at least every 500 cartridges in normal conditions. Changing the HUB tapered mount is a configuration job in SIG's book, not part of its cleaning, and is not in this guide.

steps.title: ⛔ Host unloaded, chamber checked by eye AND by touch
steps.action: Before the can comes off, make the host rifle safe the way its own manual says: unloaded, with the chamber both looked into and felt. SIG asks for this every time a suppressor is installed, tightened or removed.
steps.prose: Both hands are about to be at the muzzle. This book covers the suppressor, not the rifle; for unloading the host, SIG sends you to the host's own operator's manual.
steps.quote: ALWAYS ENSURE THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND CLEARED BY VISUALLY AND PHYSICALLY INSPECTING THE CHAMBER PRIOR TO INSTALLING, TIGHTENING, OR REMOVING A SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 3.1 ATTACHING SUPPRESSOR, WARNING UNLOAD/CLEAR, p.17

steps.title: ⛔ Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: Keep your hands off the suppressor until it has cooled. A can that has just been shot is hot enough to burn bare skin, and it looks no different from a cold one.
steps.prose: Wait it out. Nothing in this guide is urgent enough to justify a burn.
steps.quote: NEVER TOUCH SUPPRESSOR WHEN HOT. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY RESULT IN SEVERE BURNS TO UNPROTECTED SKIN.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 4.0 REMOVING SUPPRESSOR FROM FIREARM, WARNING HOT SURFACE, p.24
steps.warn: NEVER TOUCH SUPPRESSOR WHEN HOT. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY RESULT IN SEVERE BURNS TO UNPROTECTED SKIN.

steps.title: Break it loose with a 7/8-in. wrench
steps.action: Hold the rifle the way SIG asks, with the proper vise and action rod, put a 7/8-in. wrench on the mount end of the suppressor and turn it counter-clockwise until it will turn by hand.
steps.prose: It went on torqued, so it will not start by hand. SIG warns that the wrong equipment here can damage the receiver; if you cannot hold the rifle that way, SIG's customer service will help with the removal.
steps.caution: ENSURE THE PROPER EQUIPMENT, VISE, AND ACTION ROD ARE USED DURING REMOVAL. FAILURE TO DO SO MAY RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE UPPER RECEIVER.
steps.quote: Using a 7/8-in. wrench, loosen the suppressor until it can be turned by hand.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 4.0 REMOVING SUPPRESSOR FROM FIREARM, step 1, p.25

steps.title: Unscrew it the rest of the way off the barrel
steps.action: Keep turning the suppressor counter-clockwise by hand until it comes off the barrel.
steps.prose: Bring it straight off the threads rather than letting it hang on the last turn. If it gets harder to break loose from one cleaning to the next, carbon is building up between the can and the muzzle, and SIG's answer is to clean there more often.
steps.caution: AS CARBON BUILDS UP BETWEEN THE SUPPRESSOR AND THE MUZZLE, IT WILL BECOME PROGRESSIVELY MORE DIFFICULT TO REMOVE THE SUPPRESSOR.
steps.quote: Continue to unscrew the suppressor from the barrel until it can be removed.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 4.0 REMOVING SUPPRESSOR FROM FIREARM, step 2, p.25

steps.title: ⛔ That is as far as it goes: no internal cleaning, no further disassembly
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart for cleaning. SIG states that the TiN CAN needs no internal cleaning, and that taking it apart beyond unscrewing its HUB tapered mount is not authorized. Everything below is work on the outside of a closed can.
steps.prose: A can SIG does not want opened is not a can you have failed to open. Damage, or a suspected baffle or end cap strike, goes to SIG's customer service.
steps.aside: ENDURE and TINCAN suppressors do not require any internal cleaning.
steps.quote: FURTHER DISASSEMBLY OF THE SUPPRESSOR IS NOT AUTHORIZED. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY DAMAGE SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 6.1 REMOVAL, CAUTION, p.30

steps.title: Clean the suppressor's threads: nylon brush, never steel
steps.action: Clean any residue off the suppressor's threads. Use a nylon brush on carbon; a steel wire brush can damage the Cerakote finish.
steps.prose: Clean threads are what let the can come off next time without a fight.
steps.quote: Clean the suppressor threads of any residue buildup.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 5.1 CLEANING, step 1, p.27
steps.warn: DO NOT USE A STEEL WIRE BRUSH AS IT CAN DAMAGE THE CERAKOTE FINISH OF THE SUPRESSOR. USE A NYLON BRUSH FOR REMOVING CARBON BUILDUP.

steps.title: Wipe the body with CLP, then wipe it dry
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the suppressor body with a rag moistened with CLP to take off any residue, then wipe the body dry.
steps.prose: This is a wipe, not a soak. SIG cautions that solvents can harm the surface finish and against over-lubricating, and nothing goes inside the can.
steps.quote: Wipe the suppressor body with a rag moistened with CLP to remove any residue. Wipe the body dry.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 5.1 CLEANING, step 2, p.27

steps.title: Clean the rifle's muzzle threads: solvent only, no CLP, no lube
steps.action: Clean residue off the rifle's muzzle threads with a brush and a dry cleaning solvent similar to the one SIG names (MIL-P-D-680). Put no CLP or other lubricant on the barrel threads.
steps.prose: This is the one place SIG says no to CLP: the body gets a CLP wipe, the barrel threads get solvent and go back bare. Work with eye protection on and the room ventilated.
steps.quote: Clean any residue buildup from the rifle's muzzle threads with a brush and a dry cleaning solvent similar to (MIL-P-D-680). Do not use CLP or any other lubricant on the barrel threads.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 5.1 CLEANING, step 3, p.27
steps.warn: READ AND FOLLOW THE MANUFACTURER’S WARNINGS BEFORE USING SOLVENTS OR CLEANERS. USE IN A WELL-VENTILATED AREA. WEAR EYE PROTECTION.

steps.title: Inspect: threads, body, and the HUB mount secure in the body
steps.action: Check the rifle's muzzle threads and the HUB mount threads for damage. Check the suppressor body for damage. Make sure the HUB mount is secure in the suppressor body.
steps.prose: If accuracy has suddenly dropped off or bullets are tumbling into the target, SIG treats that as a possible baffle or end cap strike: stop shooting, unload, check the can is tight on the barrel, and look at the end cap and body.
steps.aside: If there is damage or suspected damage contact customer service for repair.
steps.quote: Ensure the HUB mount (4) is secure in the suppressor body.
steps.cite: SIG BOLT RIFLE SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102786-01 REV05 — 5.2 INSPECTION, step 3, p.28

deepAbsentReason: SIG's bolt rifle suppressor book states that ENDURE and TINCAN suppressors do not require any internal cleaning (5.1 CLEANING, printed p.27) and, after the HUB tapered mount is unscrewed from the body, that further disassembly of the suppressor is not authorized (6.1 REMOVAL, CAUTION, printed p.30). The book prints no procedure that opens the body: its maintenance is the threads, the outside of the body and an inspection (pp.26–28), which are in the routine lane above. A can with damage or a suspected baffle or end cap strike goes to SIG: the book asks the owner to contact customer service for repair (1.9 BAFFLE STRIKE, printed p.12). This listing therefore has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: THREADS
tasks: Suppressor threads cleaned of residue buildup.
Rifle's muzzle threads cleaned with a brush and a dry cleaning solvent.
Never CLP or any other lubricant on the barrel threads.
⛔ Never a steel wire brush: it can damage the Cerakote finish.

cleaning.name: SUPPRESSOR BODY
tasks: Body wiped with a rag moistened with CLP.
Do not over-lubricate; solvents can harm the surface finish.

cleaning.name: INSPECTION
tasks: Muzzle threads and HUB mount threads checked for damage.
HUB mount secure in the suppressor body.
Damage or a suspected baffle or end cap strike: contact SIG customer service.

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ No internal cleaning and no further disassembly of the suppressor.
⛔ Nothing put into the can: no water, oil, grease, wire pulling gel, ablatives or any other liquid.
⛔ No altered, added or substituted parts.

reassembly: Host rifle unloaded, chamber checked by eye and by touch.
Threads of both the muzzle and the suppressor clean, the barrel threads with no lubricant on them.

The HUB mount in the can matches the barrel: a 90 degree mount only on a barrel with a 90 degree shoulder, a tapered mount only on a tapered barrel. ⛔ Never a taper cap on a tapered barrel to make a 90 degree mount fit. If the mount is the wrong one, section 6.0 of SIG's book covers changing it.
Muzzle device clear of the baffles: measured from the flange of the HUB mount to the end of the device, less than 1.25 in. SIG recommends attaching the HUB mount directly to the barrel.
Thread the suppressor clockwise onto the barrel by hand.
With a 7/8-in. crow's foot wrench on a torque wrench handle, tighten to 25-27 ft-lbf, or to the rifle manufacturer's recommended torque value.
fncheck: With the host unloaded and the chamber checked: the suppressor is threaded on clockwise and torqued to 25-27 ft-lbf (or the rifle maker's value), its HUB mount matches the barrel's shoulder, and no muzzle device reaches the baffles. During use, check now and then that it is still securely threaded on. If it is dropped or struck, inspect it for damage straight away and make sure it is properly aligned with the barrel. SIG says titanium cans may throw visible sparks when fired, and that the sparks are not a defect. ⛔ Jacketed projectiles to SAAMI specification only: never non-jacketed, frangible, tracer, multi-projectile or shot cartridges. Never fire it with water, debris or anything else inside, never pour water or ablatives into it, and do not keep firing once it has overheated.
